newsitem.title: USA: Pegasus Gold, Dayton Mining agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Pegasus Gold, Dayton Mining agree to merge.

text.p: Pegasus Gold Inc said Monday it had signed an agreement with Dayton Mining Corp to merge.
Pegasus said it would merge with Dayton through a wholly-owned subsidiary in the $390 million agreement.
Each Dayton shareholder would be entitled to 0.75 of a Pegasus share per Dayton share, it said.
Pegasus said the merger would be complete by the end of the year.

The new company, to be called Pegasus Gold Inc, would have an estimated market capitalization of $860 million, it said. The company would have a cash flow from mining operations of $60 million in 1997, rising to more than $100 million in 1998, it added.
Pegasus said the new company's production was expected to rise from 740,000 ounces of gold in 1997 to 880,000 in 1999.
It said the merger would add shareholder value by increasing reserves and production as well as decreasing cash costs.

"Andacollo is a superior asset," said Pegasus, referring to the gold mine in Chile -- Dayton's key asset -- to be operated by the new company. "This mine has the potential to host over 3.0 million ounces of minable reserves."
Dayton said the terms of the agreement represented a 23-percent premium to its C$9.60 closing share price on September 13.
It said one of its directors, Wayne McClay, had agreed to sit on the board of Pegasus.
